questions.scenario: A security group suddenly allows SSH from the internet. Which service answers who called AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress, when, and from which identity?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records AWS API activity and caller context. Learn more in the [CloudTrail User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html).

questions.scenario: The incident team needs the security group configuration before and after the change. Which service owns that history?
questions.explanation: AWS Config records resource configuration state and relationships over time for supported resource types. Learn more in [What is AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html).

questions.scenario: A management-event trail exists, but investigators need object-level GetObject and DeleteObject evidence for a sensitive bucket. What must be enabled?

options.text: S3 data events for the relevant bucket or selectors.

questions.explanation: S3 object API activity is a CloudTrail data-event category and requires explicit selection. Learn more in the [CloudTrail User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html).

questions.scenario: A team relies only on the default 90-day Event history view. What is missing for durable organization-wide evidence and analysis?

options.text: A trail or CloudTrail Lake event data store with appropriate selectors, encryption, retention, and central ownership.

questions.explanation: Durable and organization-wide collection requires an intentionally configured trail or event data store. Learn more in the [CloudTrail User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html).

questions.scenario: An exposure alarm fires shortly after an unknown infrastructure change. Which sequence supports a strong What changed investigation?

options.text: Use Config history to identify the changed resource state and time window.
Treat a missing Config snapshot as proof that no API call occurred.
Use CloudTrail to identify the API call and principal.
Make the affected resource public so configuration changes are easier to see.
Correlate the change with deployment and alarm evidence.

questions.explanation: Config and CloudTrail answer complementary questions, and operational evidence ties the change to impact. Missing evidence in one source is not proof of absence. Learn more in [AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html) and [CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html).
